passage.label: Among his kind was Abraham, when he came to his Lord with a sound heart; he said to his father and his people what do you worship, is it falsehood as gods other than Allah you desire, then what is your thought about the Lord of the worlds; he cast a look at the stars and said indeed I am about to be ill, so they turned away departing; he turned to their gods saying do you not eat, what is wrong with you that you do not speak, and turned upon them a blow with his right hand; the people came hastening; he said do you worship that which you yourselves carve while Allah created you and that which you do; they said construct for him a furnace and throw him into the burning fire; they intended a plan but We made them the most debased; he said indeed I will go to my Lord, He will guide me; my Lord grant me a child from among the righteous; We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy; when he reached with him the age of exertion he said O my son I have seen in a dream that I must sacrifice you so see what you think; he said O my father do as you are commanded, you will find me if Allah wills of the steadfast; when they had both submitted and he put him down upon his forehead We called O Abraham you have fulfilled the vision; thus We reward the doers of good; this was the clear trial; We ransomed him with a great sacrifice; left favorable mention among later generations; peace upon Abraham; thus We reward the doers of good; he was of Our believing servants; We gave him good tidings of Isaac a prophet from among the righteous; We blessed him and Isaac, but among their descendants is the doer of good and the clearly unjust to himself

arabicExcerpts.text: إِذۡ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوۡمِهِۦ مَاذَا تَعۡبُدُونَ
فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِهِمۡ فَقَالَ أَلَا تَأۡكُلُونَ
قَالُواْ ٱبۡنُواْ لَهُۥ بُنۡيَٰنٗا فَأَلۡقُوهُ فِي ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
وَقَالَ إِنِّي ذَاهِبٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّي سَيَهۡدِينِ

فَلَمَّا بَلَغَ مَعَهُ ٱلسَّعۡيَ قَالَ يَٰبُنَيَّ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰ فِي ٱلۡمَنَامِ أَنِّيٓ أَذۡبَحُكَ فَٱنظُرۡ مَاذَا تَرَىٰۚ قَالَ يَـٰٓأَبَتِ ٱفۡعَلۡ مَا تُؤۡمَرُۖ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِينَ
قَدۡ صَدَّقۡتَ ٱلرُّءۡيَآۚ إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
وَبَٰرَكۡنَا عَلَيۡهِ وَعَلَىٰٓ إِسۡحَٰقَۚ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِمَا مُحۡسِنٞ وَظَالِمٞ لِّنَفۡسِهِۦ مُبِينٞ

mainSubject.label: Ibrahim introduced as of Nuh's kind, approaching his Lord with a sound heart; the paternal and communal interrogation exposing idol-worship as desired falsehood and pressing the question of the Lord of the worlds; the star-glance and illness statement enabling the private confrontation with silent, non-eating idols and the right-hand blow; the carving argument that Allah created both the worshippers and their works; the furnace plot reversed into the plotters' debasement; emigration under promised guidance and the supplication for righteous offspring answered by tidings of a forbearing boy; the dream-sacrifice dialogue at the age of exertion met with filial compliance conditioned on Allah's will; mutual submission and the forehead placement followed by the call declaring the vision fulfilled; the clear trial resolved by ransom with a great sacrifice; lasting mention, peace and the muhsin-believing-servant formula; tidings of Isaac and blessing whose descendants divide into the doer of good and the self-unjust
